evidence.note: Joktan fathers the children listed here. Hadoram appears immediately before Uzal in verse 27, and verse 29 calls them all sons of Joktan.

article.name: הֲדוֹרָם
article.summary: Genesis names Hadoram among the sons of Joktan.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for הֲדוֹרָם. Leave the root unassigned because the passage supplies no evidence for deriving the name from הדה.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:26–29 names Hadoram among Joktan’s sons.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:27 lists Hadoram alongside Uzal and Diklah. Genesis 10:29 identifies all those listed as sons of Joktan. The genealogy identifies the bearer and gives no explanation of the name’s origin.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no attached prefix or suffix. The preceding וְאֶת is a separate word that marks Hadoram as another direct object of יָלַד in Genesis 10:26.
analysis.sense: The personal name of a son of Joktan.

evidence.note: Verse 27 names Uzal between Hadoram and Diklah in the list that verse 29 identifies as Joktan’s sons.

article.name: אוּזָל
article.summary: Uzal is one of the sons of Joktan. The derivation of his name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Uzal with the root unassigned.
draft.definition: Uzal is the personal name of a son of Joktan.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:26–29 identifies Uzal by his father and gives no explanation of the name’s derivation.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:26 names Joktan as the father. Verse 27 lists Uzal between Hadoram and Diklah, and verse 29 identifies all those listed as Joktan’s sons.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. The preceding וְאֶת is a separate word marking Uzal as another direct object of יָלַד, “fathered,” in Genesis 10:26.

draft.change: Refresh the occurrence’s reference to word 0 of article 2t. The current definite-object sense already cites Genesis 10:27 for Diklah.
draft.definition: Introduces a definite direct object, here a person identified by name.
draft.evidence: וְאֶת דִּקְלָה adds Diklah to the objects of יָלַד in the genealogy of Joktan.

analysis.evidence: The final וְאֶת introduces דִּקְלָה, “Diklah,” adding him to the sons whom Joktan fathered. The governing verb is יָלַד, “fathered,” in Genesis 10:26.
analysis.morphology: וְ is the prefixed coordinating conjunction “and.” אֶת is the unsuffixed direct-object particle.
analysis.sense: Marks Diklah as a definite direct object.

evidence.note: Joktan is the father in verse 26, Diklah is named in verse 27, and verse 29 identifies the people listed as Joktan’s sons.

article.name: דִּקְלָה
article.summary: Diklah is named immediately after Uzal among the sons of Joktan. The genealogy does not explain his name.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Diklah. The verbal gloss supplied with the token does not fit its use in the genealogy.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:26–29 names Diklah among Joktan’s sons, immediately after Uzal.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:26 introduces the list with “Joktan fathered.” In verse 27, וְאֶת introduces Hadoram, Uzal and Diklah in turn as objects of that verb. Verse 29 identifies them all as sons of Joktan. The genealogy gives no derivation for the name.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun. The preceding וְאֶת is a separate word. The final ה belongs to the name.
analysis.sense: The personal name of a son of Joktan.
